title: Tenant fencing with dynamic priority weighting and backpressure
creator: Ava Thompson
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity report intermittent tail-latency spikes and throughput drops when co-located workloads exhibit bursty KV-cache or memory pressure. Current lease-based quotas provide coarse isolation but do not gracefully degrade lower-priority tenants or provide deterministic throughput guarantees under correlated bursts.

Proposal: Implement a tenant fencing controller that applies dynamic priority-weighted guarantees and coordinated backpressure across the GPU serving stack. Key components: (1) admission-stage priority weights attached to each tenant's queue; (2) short-window adaptive smoothing that converts burst signals (KV cache misses, kernel saturation, memory bandwidth contention) into proportional throttle tokens; (3) soft-fence lane allocation enabling guaranteed baseline throughput while allowing bounded burst reclaiming based on spare capacity; (4) transparent fallback paths that route degraded requests to cheaper/compatible model variants when sustained contention occurs.

Goals & acceptance criteria:
- Baseline per-tenant throughput guarantee configurable per-reservation (e.g., 50 rps @ 100 tokens/s) that persists under typical co-tenancy.
- Under a noisy-neighbor event, lower-priority tenants should see smooth degradation (latency increases within SLO budget) instead of hard eviction > 90% of the time in internal chaos tests.
- Autoscaler hooks: the controller must surface a demand signal that triggers reserved autoscale actions within 60s for sustained headroom loss.
- Observability: dashboard panels showing weight adjustments, token burn rate, eviction predictions and per-tenant SLA breach projections.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Hard slices vs soft fences: chosen soft-fence design preserves bin-packing efficiency while bounding worst-case degradation using rapidly-adjusting token buckets.
- Kernel-level preemption complexity vs request-level throttling: start with request-level control plus best-effort kernel hints (cgroup priorities) to reduce implementation risk.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature gate behind a dedicated-2026.04 flag and enable for an internal Dedicated cluster.
2) Run chaos bench (synthetic noisy tenants + real workloads) for two cycles; tune smoothing window and reclaim policy.
3) Gradual customer opt-in: select enterprise customers with reserved capacity and a test window for telemetry validation.

Telemetry & SLOs to capture:
- per-tenant weight, token bucket occupancy, throttle events, mean/99 latency, throughput, and model-fallback counts.
- regression alerting threshold: 3x increase in 99p latency or >10% sustained throughput drop for 5m.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for controller math and policy transitions.
- e2e integration test with the serving runtime that simulates KV cache miss storms and memory blowouts.
- Load tests to verify autoscaler trigger accuracy and guard against oscillation.
